target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Changes

- **`src/acp/client.ts`** — replace `!("sessionUpdate" in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate")` (1 line)

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — Object.hasOwn on ACP session notification data

The proof script mirrors the exact `printSessionUpdate` logic and exercises it against realistic ACP `SessionNotification` objects matching the `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` schema (where `sessionUpdate` is a required discriminator const on every `SessionUpdate` union arm).

```text
$ node scripts/proof-99363-printSessionUpdate.mjs
==============================================================
Proof: PR #99363 — Object.hasOwn in printSessionUpdate
==============================================================

📋 Test 1: All ACP sessionUpdate discriminator variants
--------------------------------------------------
  [agentMessageChunk] → matched=true, action="write text to stdout"
  ✅ PASS: agentMessageChunk: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCall] → matched=true, action="log tool read_file (in_progress)"
  ✅ PASS: toolCall: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [toolCallUpdate] → matched=true, action="log update tool_001: completed"
  ✅ PASS: toolCallUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [availableCommandsUpdate] → matched=true, action="log commands: /help /status"
  ✅ PASS: availableCommandsUpdate: should match (has sessionUpdate own-property)
  [nonSessionUpdate] → matched=false, action="undefined"
  ✅ PASS: nonSessionUpdate: should NOT match (no sessionUpdate)

📋 Test 2: Object.hasOwn vs `in` operator — own-property equivalence
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): true
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true
  ✅ PASS: Both return true for own property

📋 Test 3: Prototype pollution safety — Object.hasOwn advantage
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.prototype.sessionUpdate injected → "agent_message_chunk"
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false ← correctly rejects injected
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               true ← incorrectly matches injected
  ✅ PASS: Object.hasOwn correctly REJECTS prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: in operator INCORRECTLY matches prototype-injected property
  ✅ PASS: Object.prototype.sessionUpdate removed after cleanup

📋 Test 4: Missing property — both operators agree
--------------------------------------------------
  Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate"): false
  "sessionUpdate" in update:               false
  ✅ PASS: Both return false for missing property

==============================================================
Results: 10 passed, 0 failed out of 10 assertions
==============================================================

✅ PROOF PASSED — Object.hasOwn behavior is correct for ACP session updates.

Key findings:
  1. Object.hasOwn and `in` operator behave identically for normal ACP
     session update discriminator properties (all 4 update types pass).
  2. Object.hasOwn correctly rejects non-session-update notifications
     that lack a sessionUpdate own property.
  3. Object.hasOwn provides prototype pollution safety: unlike `in`,
     it does NOT match a prototype-injected sessionUpdate property.
  4. The ACP SDK schema requires sessionUpdate as a required discriminator
     on every SessionUpdate union arm — so in practice both are equivalent,
     but Object.hasOwn is the more defensive, semantically correct choice.
```

## Related

N/A (self-contained code hygiene improvement)
